presenceLabel: Caborn-Welborn area (archaeological culture, not a tribe)
presenceNote: An archaeological culture, not a tribe: late Mississippian villages near the mouth of the Wabash River that archaeologists group as Caborn-Welborn, about AD 1400–1700. Drawn: Union and Henderson counties, Kentucky, and Posey County, Indiana. A general area, not a boundary; no site locations are shown. High confidence for years, medium for area.
overlapNote: The same Kentucky counties hold older Mississippian and Green River Archaic sites, but in other centuries. Its years overlap the Mosopelea (1673–84) and Illinois and Miami areas, which lie elsewhere. No descent from or link to any later people is claimed.
basis: Kentucky Archaeological Survey / Kentucky Heritage Council Mississippi-period chapter and Wikipedia (Caborn-Welborn culture). Public agency sources.

eras.label: 1400–1700 CE · Ohio and Wabash rivers
eras.text: Caborn-Welborn is an archaeological culture, a group of sites that archaeologists define from the pottery, village layouts and dates they share; it is not a tribe, and no descent from or link to any later people is claimed. The Kentucky Archaeological Survey reports more than 80 sites in a four-county area along the Ohio River in Kentucky, Indiana and Illinois, 52 of them in Henderson and Union counties, Kentucky, and dates the culture to about AD 1400–1700. The tint is Union and Henderson counties plus Posey County, Indiana, where Wikipedia lists sites. The sources used here do not name the fourth county, so it is not drawn; this is a general area, not a boundary, and no site locations are shown. The survey notes it is unlikely that this culture can be tied to a historically documented tribe.
